title: Structural tension: the unique log-N counterterm (3 c_{N,2} l_N) is shift-invariant, so the separating divergence must live in a 'no-renormalization' term

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** `rem:masstype`, `prop:ctvar`, `lem:std`(ii), `lem:noBgamma`.

This sharpens q1-13/q1-14 into a structural diagnosis the solver must confront.

The solution proves (carefully, via order-5/3/1 chaos bookkeeping) that the **unique** $\log N$-divergent counterterm in the renormalized cube is $3c_{N,2}\mathbf l_N$, attached to the **first-chaos** field $\mathbf l=\ell$, which is **invariant** under $u\mapsto u+\psi$. Combined with `lem:noBgamma`, this yields a closed loop:

- If $3c_{N,2}\mathbf l_N$ is the only $\log N$ object, and it is shift-invariant, then no cube-derived observable can pick up a $\log N$ from the shift (confirmed by eq. `eq:Fshift`: $F_N(u+\psi)-F_N(u)\to 3\mathbf q\circ\psi+\text{finite}$, no $c_{N,2}$).

Therefore the separating deterministic $c_{N,2}\langle\psi,\psi\rangle$ **cannot** come from the cube's renormalization at all; it must originate in a term the solution currently labels **'convergent, no renormalization'**. The prime suspect: under the shift the *squared* field becomes $u+\psi$, so $H_2(P_N(u+\psi);c_N)=H_2(P_Nu;c_N)+2\psi_N P_Nu+\psi_N^2$. The cross-term $2\psi_N P_Nu$, when its $P_Nu$ leg is resonated/contracted against the cube or $\mathbf C$ data, produces a **deterministic** contraction $\sim c_{N,2}\psi_N$ that has **no $\mu$-analogue** (it requires the deterministic $\psi$ leg to be one of the contracted legs). The solver must (i) identify exactly which term carries this survivor, (ii) verify it is genuinely absent under $\mu$, and (iii) confirm it is not removable by any $\psi$-independent counterterm. Until this is done, the chaos analysis is internally consistent but proves the WRONG thing (no separation).
